items.excerpt: Michael La Ronn and Sacha Black answer member questions on where AI editing actually helps and where it fails, plus IngramSpark's return and series cover consistency.
Spotify is rolling out AI-powered audiobook playlists, a voice chatbot, and one-click series continuation, changing how indie audiobooks get discovered.
Dan Holloway covers Self-Publishing Partnership's collapse and unpaid royalties, alongside what Anthropic's new Claude watermark means for authors who draft with AI.
Google Play Books' AI-driven Book Insights has launched for thousands of select English titles. Google did not say if or when the tool will expand to non-English books.
A rundown of every audiobook feature Spotify has shipped in recent months, including AI playlist generation, a conversational book chatbot and series tracking.
As AI licensing, microdeals, and expansion into new territories and formats proliferate, publishers need new rights-tracking practice to keep creators' trust.
Digital Publishing Report's annual survey asks which publishing technologies — AI tooling among them — executives should watch, pilot, or scale this year.
Analyst Carlo Carrenho's weekly round-up of international publishing headlines, including the week's AI, audiobook and rights stories.
Most published authors have, without their knowledge or consent, contributed to the AI tools that threaten their livelihoods. A plain-language guide to where the law actually stands.
STM chief executive Caroline Sutton says publishers must pair automated screening with human oversight when investigating potentially fraudulent research submissions.
New features let listeners auto-generate audiobook playlists from a prompt, ask natural-language questions about a book's contents, and track titles in a series.
Book Riot's reader survey on 'what counts as AI-written' finds no consensus — readers are far more forgiving of grammar tools than of LLMs in the editing phase.
Anthropic introduces watermarks, journalists test AI-detection tools, and Claude generates a novel about writing a novel with Claude.
Claude introduces watermarks, Substack adopts Pangram AI detection for writers, and more AI-related publishing news.
Commentators find it problematic that Claude's watermark is applied when the model is used for assistive tasks rather than purely generative ones — a direct issue for authors who edit with AI.
The reporters behind the AirTag investigation explain how Amazon buys and destructively scans rare books to build AI training corpora.
Games Workshop now has narrators read an anti-AI-training warning aloud at the top of Warhammer 40,000 audiobooks — a new front-matter convention for protecting publisher IP in audio.
